s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient in their 20s without noteworthy medical history
Presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Experienced palpitations and symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival with decreased blood pressure
Troponin T elevated at 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide elevated at 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein elevated at 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin elevated at 39.68 ng/mL
Severe left ventricular dysfunction on transthoracic echocardiography with ejection fraction 38%
Wall motion abnormalities in multiple vascular territories on echocardiography
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

ECG findings: upward QRS complex in lead aVR, pure R wave in leads V1 and V2, sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T and ST-segment elevation on ECG, but normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography, with a potential trigger of upper respiratory tract infection

shortlist.label: Giant cell myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, elevated inflammatory markers, and hemodynamic instability

shortlist.label: Fulminant lymphocytic myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, elevated inflammatory markers, and rapid progression to hemodynamic instability

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, dyspnea, and recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms, along with elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, and severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography, is most consistent with myocarditis. The absence of coronary artery disease on angiography and the pattern of ECG changes also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Lack of a clear stressor and the presence of severe left ventricular dysfunction with wall motion abnormalities in multiple vascular territories make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Giant cell myocarditis
rejected.why: This condition is rare and typically presents with more severe and rapid progression of heart failure, which is not clearly evident in this case

rejected.label: Fulminant lymphocytic myocarditis
rejected.why: While this is a severe form of myocarditis, the presentation and laboratory findings in this case do not specifically distinguish it from other forms of myocarditis
